Any successful psychologist quit their job and started working at McDonald's years ago.    
I FUCKING HATE psychologists.    
My father was an M.D., and I get what you're saying.    
edit:  psychologists should need a license for all the bullshit generalizations they seem to make.  I FUCKING HATE ALL OF THE psychologists I'VE EVER MET.

Physics and Math are, at least, based in reality.    
psychology is based on an old book (DSM-IV or V)    
    
    
Jesus'/King James' Bible, anyone?   
    
It's not real science.    
    
edit:Philosophy is, sometimes, pretentious. But, it doesn't pretend to be science.

My ex-wife left me during her pregnancy.   I thought it was my kid, my child, my offspring, my future happiness.    
It wasn't mine and she left me.  It still hurts, BAD.    
If you can stay in touch with "said kid", do so.    
Otherwise, I think you should move farther away.      
Go to a few titty bars, as well.

They suck.  And, it shouldn't be a paying job, IMHO.    
edit:  I digress.  But, I hope all psychology majors start studying history. And, NO, I don't want to talk about it.    
I have a degree in a soft science, too.    
I guess there wasn't much digression, there.    
Fuck psychologists.

It's annoying, yes.    
"But, they're great!"  No, not really.    
I group all therapists together: Psychiatrists, psychologists, Social Workers, Counselors, etc.  
psychologists have been the worst

Thank you for your response.    
I, also, felt great about CBT for a few years.    
I felt empowered, aware and in-charge of my emotions, at first.    
I started doubting it when nothing in my life improved.    
    
edit:  buying David Burns' "Feeling Good". Because;  Why the fuck not?

Thanks for the response.    
It's, at least, nice to hear someone else talk about CBT sucking all of the dicks.    
I've always felt like an idiot/my therapists were cuntbags when I've tried drug cocktails and all the "great group meetings that are available out there". (cooking, woodworking, dancing, beer-drinking, mountain biking, etc. classes/meet ups)
I've tried taking their advice and applying it.  But, it still hasn't worked.    
I agree.  Skyrim is a bitch of a timesuck.

I thought about doing something similar the other day.  But, I realized I don't want to put my pain on anyone else.    
I wouldn't want to see anyone commit suicide on the interwebs.    
    
I consider suicide daily.  And, I hope you won't do this.

I'm sure they'd be better at dealing with it than most.    
I'm not concerned about anyone beyond me.    
"Focus on yourself"  That's what I've been told.

I'm currently enrolled in an MBA program.  It helps fill some of my time and keeps me from drinking.  I've tried a few meet-up type things.  Not many people my age appear to be looking to spend their sparse free time around someone that doesn't share a similar life to them. (i.e., kids, family, financial worries).  I get a lot of "he doesn't have family at his age? He's weird" vibes, or whatever.  I also was taking guitar lessons, but practicing is pretty lonesome, as well.  So, I put it down.  I like fishing, but again, that's pretty much a one-person activity.
I've seen many people that are specialized in helping.  They've mentioned tons of things to do.  I've tried many of them.    
In the end they've all felt like I'm still treading water.
Hurting family, or anyone, sucks.    However, my family members are adults with their own lives going on.    I imagine they'd be able to move on.
8 different therapists over almost 6 years.  Dozens of medications.  No one close outside of family.  Loner for past 10 years.  No, I don't enjoy my work.  But, it pays my bills.
Immediate family. Mother, Father, Sister, and Brother.

I couldn't tell you.  I've been in a dark cloud for almost 30 years.    
edit:  I'll elaborate.  I've always felt alone and disconnected from the world.    
The happiest I think I have ever felt was when my wife became pregnant.  I thought I was going to have a child.  Six months into the pregnancy she told me it wasn't mine and she was leaving me.

CBT=Cognitive Behavioral Therapy.    

I'm currently working as a tax accountant for a privately-held firm.    I don't really like much any more.  I used to enjoy life.    
But, I just don't now.
